bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to create and run workflows could supply the Git node with a staged working repository whose configured push remote was another attacker-controlled local repository. For push and pushTags, vulnerable releases left Git's file transport enabled, causing local git-receive-pack to run receive-side hooks in the target repository as the n8n process. Setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null on the initiating repository did not suppress hooks in that local receive target. The fix validates configured remotes and removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL for write operations when hooks are disabled.
flaw_origin: The original Git node accepted a workflow-selected baseDirectory, constructed simple-git for that repository, and exposed git.push() without restricting repository-controlled local remote targets or Git's file transport. That original trust-boundary crossing, rather than a later move, import, refactor, or aggregate landing, is the flaw origin.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5` shows author and committer Jan Oberhauser <jan.oberhauser@gmail.com> and the complete message `:sparkles: Add Git-Node`; the BIC commit object has no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-rcv6-pvrj-4xcg states that staging a crafted local repository lets authenticated workflow authors execute Git hooks and names patched releases 1.123.67, 2.31.5, and 2.32.1. BIC checks in a scratch object store fetched from refs/pull/1820/head: `git cat-file -p f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5` gives direct parent 06dd4236482d345b1193b87b993c944b117698bd and the human-only commit object described in ai_marker; `git diff --name-status 06dd4236482d345b1193b87b993c944b117698bd f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 -- packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts` reports `A`; and `git grep` at the BIC finds workflow parameter baseDirectory, simpleGit(gitOptions), and `await git.push()`. The PR-head tree 822bfe379a93c1ab13bbaf98f5a9e5078f95c0c6 equals the public 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb tree, while that public commit message lists many constituent changes, so the squash aggregate is rejected in favor of f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5. `git log n8n@0.122.3..n8n@0.123.0 -- packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts` locates that squash landing at the introduction boundary. The assigned fix_sha disagreement was primary 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 versus reviewer f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f. `git cat-file -p` identifies 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 as `chore: Bundle/2.x (#34680)` on main history; `git name-rev` places it at n8n@2.33.0~216. In contrast, f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f is explicitly `backport to release-candidate/2.32.x (#34692)` and `git name-rev` places it at n8n@2.32.1~1. Boundary logs show three parallel release-line landings: 1cd2c5fb22a906058cc083c3af2d561ce7f4332d in n8n@1.123.66..n8n@1.123.67, f6cb6cf3ab177c3740a5ef624b89bae5165405a1 in n8n@2.31.4..n8n@2.31.5, and f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f in n8n@2.32.0..n8n@2.32.1. Direct diffs across all three edges add `isWriteOperation` and change GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL to omit file for push/pushTags when hooks are disabled, exactly matching the advisory boundaries. Fetching refs/pull/34680/head and walking its members finds 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d as the sole member affecting Git.node.ts; `git show` for that path changes blob 9afd4a92 to 14fc1e34, exactly the same blobs and patch as public main landing 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 and the 2.32 backport. Thus 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 is the canonical main-history fix landing, while 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d is its retained direct PR member; the reviewer incorrectly promoted one of three equivalent backports to fix_sha and put the aggregate main landing in direct_fix_sha.
reasoning: The causal vulnerability was already complete in the first atomic PR member: repository-controlled configuration could direct an unrestricted push to a local receive target whose hooks execute in the n8n process. The immediate parent lacks the Git node, and the later public squash, subsequent operation additions, moves, imports, and hardening changes are not smaller introducers. The fix disagreement resolves in the primary's favor. A canonical fix_sha must identify the public main-history remediation rather than arbitrarily selecting the 2.32 backport when equivalent 1.x and 2.31.x backports also establish the advisory's release boundaries. Commit 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 is that main landing; because it is a bundle squash rather than the direct patch provenance, direct_fix_sha is decomposed to PR #34680 member 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d, the smallest retained public member affecting Git.node.ts. The BIC alone controls attribution, and its commit object has no AI signal, so later bot or AI trailers on fix bundles do not affect the NOT_AI verdict.
